originalTitle: Trump homeland security chief says ICE agents could be sent to polling places
summary: Markwayne Mullin says officers could be deployed ‘if there is a threat to that polling place or we’re serving a warrant’
content: US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin on Tuesday said that federal immigration and customs enforcement (ICE) officers could be deployed to polling sites across the country. Speaking to reporters in New York, Mullin said: “ICE isn’t there to patrol the polling places. We’re there to enforce specific threats.” For months, Democrats and voting rights groups have warned that the Trump administration might attempt to deploy federal agents to polling locations in an effort to intimidate voters and depress turnout ahead of the November midterm elections. Although the White House has downplayed such suggestions, Donald Trump has declined to rule it out while continuing to sow doubt about the integrity of past – and future – US elections. “The only reason why we would be at polling places is if there is a threat to that polling place or we’re serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down,” Mullin said. “ICE’s job is immigration, customs enforcement. That’s their job … if we’re serving a warrant we will be where we need to be.” Federal law prohibits military personnel or other “armed” agents from being “at any place where a general or special election is held”. In a separate statement to Politico, the homeland security department said: “ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations. ICE conducts intelligence-driven targeted enforcement, and if an active public safety threat endangered a polling location, they may be arrested as a result of that targeted enforcement action.” The Guardian has contacted the DHS for additional comment. Mullin’s latest comments follow statements he made in July, when he threatened to withhold federal aid from states that refused to comply with homeland security election directives as part of the administration’s crackdown on what it alleges is widespread voter fraud. “We will scrub all election records, looking for illegal aliens and those who are ineligible to vote, including those that somehow voted, yet they were deceased,” Mullin said earlier this summer, adding: “If states want the grant funding, to recap, they must secure the election.” Yet experts say the administration has failed to offer any proof for its claims of non-citizen voting. In one instance, DHS officials claimed that there may have been as many as 16,000 non-citizens registered to vote in Nevada, but later admitted they could confirm that only 185 of those people were actually non-citizens, according to records obtained by the Guardian. Meanwhile, Dan Caine, chair of the joint chiefs of staff, recently wrote in a letter that the US military had no plans to deploy troops to polling sites during the upcoming November midterm elections. Caine’s letter came in response to a request for information from senator Elissa Slotkin amid concerns that the Trump administration could send US military personnel to patrol polling sites. In his letter to Slotkin, Caine said: “The joint force has no plans to send federal military personnel or federalized members of the national guard to polling places during the 2026 elections.” He added that there were “no plans to use such personnel to seize ballots, voting machines, or other election-related material”.
chineseTitle: 特朗普国土安全部负责人表示，ICE特工可能会被派往投票站
chineseSummary: 马克韦恩·穆林 (Markwayne Mullin) 表示，“如果投票站受到威胁或者我们正在执行逮捕令”，则可以部署警察
chineseContent: 美国国土安全部长马克韦恩·穆林周二表示，联邦移民和海关执法局（ICE）官员可能会被部署到全国各地的投票站。马林在纽约接受记者采访时表示：“ICE 不是来巡逻投票站的。我们是来执行特定威胁的。”几个月来，民主党人和投票权组织一直警告称，特朗普政府可能会尝试向投票地点部署联邦特工，以在 11 月中期选举之前恐吓选民并抑制投票率。尽管白宫淡化了此类建议，但唐纳德·特朗普拒绝排除这种可能性，同时继续对过去和未来美国选举的公正性提出质疑。马林说：“我们出现在投票站的唯一原因是该投票站是否受到威胁，或者我们正在对我们一直在积极追踪的人发出逮捕令。” “ICE 的工作是移民、海关执法。这就是他们的工作……如果我们执行搜查令，我们就会到达我们需要到达的地方。”联邦法律禁止军事人员或其他“武装”特工“出现在举行大选或特别选举的任何地方”。在给 Politico 的另一份声明中，国土安全部表示：“ICE 并未计划针对投票地点的行动。ICE 进行情报驱动的有针对性的执法，如果活跃的公共安全威胁危及投票地点，他们可能会因该有针对性的执法行动而被捕。” 《卫报》已联系国土安全部征求更多评论。穆林的最新评论是在他7月份发表的声明之后发表的，当时他威胁要停止向那些拒绝遵守国土安全选举指令的州提供联邦援助。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
